title: Technology in Our Lives
description: Use technology habits and present forms to explain and handle ideas related to technology in our lives with appropriate B1 complexity.
objectives: Use technology habits and present forms to explain and handle ideas related to technology in our lives with appropriate B1 complexity.

stages.title: Understand meaning and form
stages.instructions: Read the concept, pattern, examples, contrast, common issue, and recap.

blocks.text: The communicative aim of this lesson is to use technology habits and present forms to explain and handle ideas related to technology in our lives with appropriate B1 complexity. The central language focus is technology habits and present forms. In the context of technology, media & opinions, form and meaning work together: first identify the relationship between the ideas, then choose wording that makes that relationship clear to another person. At B1, connected communication matters more than isolated accuracy. Give the main information, link events or reasons, and respond to a follow-up without relying on memorized one-line answers.

blocks.english: We should consider digital tool carefully.
blocks.explanation: This model establishes the main communicative move.
This model develops or qualifies the message.

blocks.text: Start with the model “We should consider digital tool carefully.” It establishes a useful direction for the exchange. The second model, “The discussion highlighted stay connected.” adds another layer: a reason, implication, contrast, or response. Notice how each complete chunk does a communicative job. Practice replacing one detail while preserving the original grammar, stance, and register. Then connect the revised sentence to a relevant consequence or example instead of changing topic abruptly.

A useful pattern for this lesson is: technology habits and present forms. Use it when the situation genuinely calls for that meaning. Contrast matters: a direct factual statement presents information, while a qualified or hypothetical form changes the speaker's commitment to it. The choice should be driven by evidence, time reference, relationship, and purpose. In listening, pay attention not only to individual words but also to linkers, stress, and the speaker's degree of certainty.

blocks.title: Contrast
blocks.text: Compare a direct statement with language shaped by technology habits and present forms; the intended meaning determines the form.

A common issue is to select an advanced-looking form without maintaining its meaning across the sentence. That can create a mismatch in time, stance, or register. Check three things: what happened or is being proposed, how certain the speaker is, and what response is expected. For technology in our lives, clarity comes from a coherent message rather than maximum complexity. The later stages recycle the same vocabulary and expressions so that recognition becomes controlled production and then flexible interaction.

blocks.title: Common issue
blocks.text: Do not add complexity that changes the time reference, degree of certainty, or relationship with the listener.
